</FONT>

<P align="right" style="font-size: 10pt">PEABODY ENERGY</FONT><BR>
<FONT style="font-size: 22pt"><B>News Release</B></FONT>



<P align="right" style="font-size: 22pt"><FONT style="font-size: 10pt">CONTACT:<BR>

(314)&nbsp;342-7768</FONT>



<P align="left" style="font-size: 10pt"><FONT style="font-size: 11pt"><U><B>FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE</B></U>
<BR>
Jan. 25, 2011
</FONT>

<P align="center" style="font-size: 11pt"><B>PEABODY ENERGY ANNOUNCES RESULTS</B><BR>
<U><B>FOR THE YEAR ENDED DECEMBER 31, 2010</B></U>



<P>
<TABLE width="100%" border="0" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="font-size: 10pt">

<TR valign="top" style="font-size: 11pt; color: #000000; background: transparent">
    <TD width="1%" nowrap align="right">&#149;</TD>
    <TD width="1%">&nbsp;</TD>
    <TD><B>2010 earnings and EBITDA second best in company history</B></TD>
</TR>

</TABLE>


<P>
<TABLE width="100%" border="0" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="font-size: 10pt">

<TR valign="top" style="font-size: 11pt; color: #000000; background: transparent">
    <TD width="1%" nowrap align="right">&#149;</TD>
    <TD width="1%">&nbsp;</TD>
    <TD><B>Diluted EPS rises 75% to $2.87; adjusted diluted EPS totals $3.05</B></TD>
</TR>

</TABLE>


<P>
<TABLE width="100%" border="0" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="font-size: 10pt">

<TR valign="top" style="font-size: 11pt; color: #000000; background: transparent">
    <TD width="1%" nowrap align="right">&#149;</TD>
    <TD width="1%">&nbsp;</TD>
    <TD><B>2010 EBITDA increases 41% to $1.82&nbsp;billion</B></TD>
</TR>

</TABLE>


<P>
<TABLE width="100%" border="0" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="font-size: 10pt">

<TR valign="top" style="font-size: 11pt; color: #000000; background: transparent">
    <TD width="1%" nowrap align="right">&#149;</TD>
    <TD width="1%">&nbsp;</TD>
    <TD><B>Operating profit climbs 57% to $1.33&nbsp;billion</B></TD>
</TR>

</TABLE>


<P>
<TABLE width="100%" border="0" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="font-size: 10pt">

<TR valign="top" style="font-size: 11pt; color: #000000; background: transparent">
    <TD width="1%" nowrap align="right">&#149;</TD>
    <TD width="1%">&nbsp;</TD>
    <TD><B>Revenues reach record $6.86&nbsp;billion</B></TD>
</TR>

</TABLE>


<P align="left" style="font-size: 11pt">ST.&nbsp;LOUIS, Jan. 25 &#150; Peabody Energy (NYSE: BTU) today reported full-year 2010 EBITDA of $1.82
billion, a 41&nbsp;percent increase over prior-year levels. Income from continuing operations rose 76
percent to $805.1&nbsp;million, with diluted earnings per share from continuing operations of $2.87.
Adjusted diluted earnings per share from continuing operations increased 59&nbsp;percent to $3.05. The
company also set a new record for revenues of $6.86&nbsp;billion on sales of 245.9&nbsp;million tons.


<P align="left" style="font-size: 11pt; text-indent: 4%">&#147;Peabody delivered the second best year in company history, with record safety performance,
strong cost containment and margin expansion in every operating region,&#148; said Peabody Energy
Chairman and Chief Executive Officer Gregory H. Boyce. &#147;While heavy rains and other supply
disruptions create near-term logistics challenges, they also result in significant market upside
for Peabody&#146;s unpriced metallurgical and thermal export coal beyond the first quarter. At the same
time, our platform is in expansion mode to serve the seaborne Pacific markets, which have the
greatest sustainable growth opportunities and pricing leverage.&#148;


<P align="left" style="font-size: 11pt"><B>RESULTS FROM CONTINUING OPERATIONS</B>


<P align="left" style="font-size: 11pt; text-indent: 4%">Revenues for the full year increased $847.6&nbsp;million to $6.86&nbsp;billion, driven by higher volumes
and pricing from mining operations in both the United States and Australia. 2010 sales volumes
totaled 245.9&nbsp;million tons compared with 243.6&nbsp;million tons in 2009. Australia shipments grew 21
percent to 27&nbsp;million tons, including 9.8&nbsp;million tons of metallurgical coal and 11.1&nbsp;million tons
of seaborne thermal coal. Australian revenues rose 50&nbsp;percent on rising prices


<P align="center" style="font-size: 11pt">-More-




<P align="center" style="font-size: 10pt; display: none">1
<!-- PAGEBREAK -->




<P align="left" style="font-size: 11pt"><B>PEABODY ENERGY ANNOUNCES RESULTS &#150; PAGE 2</B>


<P align="left" style="font-size: 11pt">for both metallurgical and seaborne thermal coal. U.S. revenues increased due to higher average
realized prices in both the Midwestern and Western regions.


<P align="left" style="font-size: 11pt; text-indent: 4%">Consolidated EBITDA totaled $1.82&nbsp;billion compared with $1.29&nbsp;billion in the prior year, led
by record Mining Operations contributions.


<P>
<TABLE width="100%" border="0" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="font-size: 10pt">

<TR valign="top" style="font-size: 11pt; color: #000000; background: transparent">
    <TD width="2%" style="background: transparent">&nbsp;</TD>
    <TD width="1%" nowrap align="right">&#149;</TD>
    <TD width="1%">&nbsp;</TD>
    <TD>U.S. Mining Operations delivered EBITDA of $1.14&nbsp;billion. The company&#146;s U.S. operations
realized a 13&nbsp;percent increase in gross margins per ton on a combination of higher average
pricing and lower average costs.</TD>
</TR>

</TABLE>


<P>
<TABLE width="100%" border="0" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="font-size: 10pt">

<TR valign="top" style="font-size: 11pt; color: #000000; background: transparent">
    <TD width="2%" style="background: transparent">&nbsp;</TD>
    <TD width="1%" nowrap align="right">&#149;</TD>
    <TD width="1%">&nbsp;</TD>
    <TD>Australian Mining Operations EBITDA more than doubled prior year&#146;s results, totaling
$953.8&nbsp;million with an 82&nbsp;percent increase in gross margins per ton, despite year-end
weather-related disruptions. These impacts totaled approximately $85&nbsp;million or $0.22 per
share after tax. Fourth quarter costs per ton were also higher than average due to
weather-related production effects.</TD>
</TR>

</TABLE>


<P>
<TABLE width="100%" border="0" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="font-size: 10pt">

<TR valign="top" style="font-size: 11pt; color: #000000; background: transparent">
    <TD width="2%" style="background: transparent">&nbsp;</TD>
    <TD width="1%" nowrap align="right">&#149;</TD>
    <TD width="1%">&nbsp;</TD>
    <TD>Trading and Brokerage and Resource Management delivered a combined $101.0&nbsp;million of
EBITDA for the year. Fourth quarter Trading and Brokerage results were impacted by lower
year-over-year international brokerage earnings and weather-related declines in the
seaborne freight market and export shipments.</TD>
</TR>

</TABLE>


<P align="left" style="font-size: 11pt; text-indent: 4%">Operating profit rose 57&nbsp;percent to $1.33&nbsp;billion, leading to significant cash flow generation
of $1.09&nbsp;billion.


<P align="left" style="font-size: 11pt; text-indent: 4%">Income from continuing operations was $805.1&nbsp;million with adjusted income from continuing
operations climbing 60&nbsp;percent to $852.7&nbsp;million. Diluted earnings per share from continuing
operations reached $2.87 compared to $1.64 in the prior year, a 75&nbsp;percent increase. Full-year
adjusted diluted earnings per share rose 59&nbsp;percent to $3.05.

<P align="center" style="font-size: 10pt; display: none">2
<!-- PAGEBREAK -->




<P align="left" style="font-size: 11pt"><B>PEABODY ENERGY ANNOUNCES RESULTS &#150; PAGE 3</B>


<P align="center" style="font-size: 11pt"><U>Safety and Environmental Highlights</U>



<P align="left" style="font-size: 11pt; text-indent: 4%">Peabody also delivered its safest year in company history with a global incidence rate of 2.7
per 200,000 hours worked, 6&nbsp;percent better than the prior year. Operations earned 11 safety awards
in the United States and Australia, including being awarded the Sentinels of Safety Award by the
U.S. Department of Labor at the Farmersburg Mine for the second time in four years. The company
also earned 11 environmental awards in the United States and Mongolia.


<P align="left" style="font-size: 11pt"><B>GLOBAL COAL MARKETS AND PEABODY&#146;S POSITION</B>


<P align="left" style="font-size: 11pt; text-indent: 4%">Peabody believes the world is in the early stages of a long-term supercycle for coal as China,
India and other emerging nations dramatically increase energy use, steel consumption grows
globally, oil becomes increasingly scarce and expensive and alternatives lack the cost and scale to
effectively compete.


<P align="left" style="font-size: 11pt; text-indent: 4%">&#147;The long-term supercycle for coal is strengthening with each passing day,&#148; said Boyce.
&#147;Nations such as China and India are growing 8 to 10&nbsp;percent per year off a much larger base.
Hundreds of millions of people each year are moving to the cities, switching on technologies and
extending coal&#146;s role as the fastest growing fuel.&#148;


<P align="left" style="font-size: 11pt; text-indent: 4%">Economic growth in emerging Asia is expected to be the driver of large increases in thermal
and metallurgical coal.&nbsp; Through 2015, approximately 390 gigawatts of new coal-fueled generation
are expected to be built globally, requiring 1.2&nbsp;billion tonnes of annual coal supply.&nbsp; Global
steel production is expected to rise more than 30&nbsp;percent during that time, requiring approximately
300&nbsp;million tonnes of additional metallurgical coal supply annually.


<P align="center" style="font-size: 11pt"><U>International Markets</U>



<P align="left" style="font-size: 11pt; text-indent: 4%">Global coal markets strengthened sharply late in 2010, propelled by powerful ongoing Asian
demand growth and weather-related generation recovery in the Atlantic markets, coupled with supply
challenges across the major coal-exporting nations of the Southern Hemisphere.


<P align="left" style="font-size: 11pt; text-indent: 4%">Seaborne coal demand increased an estimated 13&nbsp;percent in 2010, led by a 32&nbsp;percent recovery
in global metallurgical coal demand.&nbsp; Pacific thermal coal demand for electricity generation rose
15&nbsp;percent in 2010, while the Atlantic market declined 10&nbsp;percent.


<P>
<TABLE width="100%" border="0" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="font-size: 10pt">

<TR valign="top" style="font-size: 11pt; color: #000000; background: transparent">
    <TD width="2%" style="background: transparent">&nbsp;</TD>
    <TD width="1%" nowrap align="right">&#149;</TD>
    <TD width="1%">&nbsp;</TD>
    <TD>Global fourth quarter demand was particularly strong in the Northern Hemisphere, where
an early and strong winter drove generation increases in Asia, Europe and North America.
Since December, heavy La Ni&#241;a-related rains have been suppressing coal supply from
Australia, Indonesia, South Africa and South America.</TD>
</TR>

</TABLE>


<P align="center" style="font-size: 11pt">-More-




<P align="center" style="font-size: 10pt; display: none">3
<!-- PAGEBREAK -->




<P align="left" style="font-size: 11pt"><B>PEABODY ENERGY ANNOUNCES RESULTS &#150; PAGE 4</B>


<P>
<TABLE width="100%" border="0" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="font-size: 10pt">

<TR valign="top" style="font-size: 11pt; color: #000000; background: transparent">
    <TD width="2%" style="background: transparent">&nbsp;</TD>
    <TD width="1%" nowrap align="right">&#149;</TD>
    <TD width="1%">&nbsp;</TD>
    <TD>Driven by record December coal imports, China&#146;s 2010 net coal imports totaled 147
million tonnes, a 41&nbsp;percent increase over 2009&#146;s previous record level.&nbsp; China&#146;s economy
grew 10&nbsp;percent in 2010 and is expected to expand another 8 to 10&nbsp;percent in 2011.</TD>
</TR>

</TABLE>


<P>
<TABLE width="100%" border="0" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="font-size: 10pt">

<TR valign="top" style="font-size: 11pt; color: #000000; background: transparent">
    <TD width="2%" style="background: transparent">&nbsp;</TD>
    <TD width="1%" nowrap align="right">&#149;</TD>
    <TD width="1%">&nbsp;</TD>
    <TD>India imports increased 25&nbsp;percent in 2010, and year-end stockpiles are less than half
of target levels.&nbsp; India&#146;s GDP increased 8&nbsp;percent in 2010 with similar growth expected in
2011.</TD>
</TR>

</TABLE>


<P>
<TABLE width="100%" border="0" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="font-size: 10pt">

<TR valign="top" style="font-size: 11pt; color: #000000; background: transparent">
    <TD width="2%" style="background: transparent">&nbsp;</TD>
    <TD width="1%" nowrap align="right">&#149;</TD>
    <TD width="1%">&nbsp;</TD>
    <TD>Australia coal exports increased 9&nbsp;percent to a record 300&nbsp;million tonnes in 2010 and
Australia remained the world&#146;s largest coal exporting nation even with December flooding.
Peabody believes seaborne coal demand will increase 6 to 8&nbsp;percent in 2011 and could exceed
1&nbsp;billion tonnes for the first time ever, driven by new generation in Asia, rebounding
economies in developed nations and continued increases in global steel production.&nbsp;</TD>
</TR>

</TABLE>


<P>
<TABLE width="100%" border="0" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="font-size: 10pt">

<TR valign="top" style="font-size: 11pt; color: #000000; background: transparent">
    <TD width="2%" style="background: transparent">&nbsp;</TD>
    <TD width="1%" nowrap align="right">&#149;</TD>
    <TD width="1%">&nbsp;</TD>
    <TD>These tight supply-demand fundamentals have driven global coal prices upward, with the
benchmark prompt thermal coal price in Newcastle rising 34&nbsp;percent in 2010 and another 10
percent since the beginning of 2011.&nbsp; The spot price for high quality hard coking coal has
exceeded $350 per tonne following settlements of $225 per tonne for the first calendar
quarter of 2011.</TD>
</TR>

</TABLE>


<P align="left" style="font-size: 11pt; text-indent: 4%">In Australia, the company has 7 to 8&nbsp;million tons of metallurgical coal available for sale in
the last three quarters of 2011; all of 2012&#146;s expected metallurgical coal sales are open to
pricing. In the seaborne thermal coal product, Peabody has 6 to 7&nbsp;million tons unpriced for 2011,
and 12 to 13&nbsp;million tons available to price in 2012.


<P align="center" style="font-size: 11pt"><U>U.S. Coal Markets</U>



<P align="left" style="font-size: 11pt; text-indent: 4%">Demand for U.S. coal rose approximately 75&nbsp;million tons in 2010, led by a 5.5&nbsp;percent increase
in coal-fueled generation and an 18&nbsp;million ton rise in exports.


<P align="left" style="font-size: 11pt; text-indent: 4%">U.S. coal generation accounted for nearly two-thirds of the growth in total power output,
outpacing natural gas and all other fuels.&nbsp; The higher coal demand was related to new coal-fueled
generation, favorable weather, and a partial reversal of 2009&#146;s coal-to-gas switching.


<P align="left" style="font-size: 11pt; text-indent: 4%">Indexed U.S. coal prices continued to rise in 2010 in all regions, with increases ranging from
30 to 50&nbsp;percent.


<P align="center" style="font-size: 11pt">-More-




<P align="center" style="font-size: 10pt; display: none">4
<!-- PAGEBREAK -->




<P align="left" style="font-size: 11pt"><B>PEABODY ENERGY ANNOUNCES RESULTS &#150; PAGE 5</B>


<P align="left" style="font-size: 11pt; text-indent: 4%">Peabody believes U.S. coal demand will increase modestly in 2011, led by colder winter weather
in the first quarter and stronger GDP growth in the back half.&nbsp; The company anticipates more
significant economic growth in 2012 and beyond, resulting from stronger consumer spending and
industrial activity.


<P align="left" style="font-size: 11pt; text-indent: 4%">Additional near-term export opportunities are developing, with favorable current economics for
Illinois and Colorado coal to Europe and Powder River Basin (PRB)&nbsp;coal to Asia and Europe.


<P align="left" style="font-size: 11pt; text-indent: 4%">In the United States, Peabody has modest amounts of coal to price in 2011, with significant
open positions in the later years to match expected higher pricing beginning in 2012. Peabody has
35 to 40&nbsp;percent available to price in 2012, and 75 to 85&nbsp;percent in 2013. The PRB, Midwest and
Colorado coal regions, where Peabody is the largest producer, are expected to both backfill Central
Appalachian supply and participate in increased export demand.


<P align="left" style="font-size: 11pt"><B>PROJECT UPDATE</B>


<P align="left" style="font-size: 11pt; text-indent: 4%">Peabody is advancing multiple organic growth projects in Australia and the United States.
Capital expenditures for 2011 are estimated in the $900 to $950&nbsp;million range, including $500 to
$550&nbsp;million earmarked for new mines, expansion and extension projects. Approximately 70&nbsp;percent
of the growth and expansion capital is targeted for Australia, with the remainder in the United
States.


<P align="left" style="font-size: 11pt; text-indent: 4%">In Australia, Peabody continues to target 35 to 40&nbsp;million tons per year of sales by 2014 to
2015, including 12 to 15&nbsp;million tons of metallurgical coal capacity and 15 to 17&nbsp;million tons of
thermal export capacity. Among the company&#146;s Australian growth projects:

coking coal Denham/Goonyella Corridor project and Wambo thermal coal expansion.</TD>
</TR>

</TABLE>


<P align="center" style="font-size: 11pt">-More-




<P align="center" style="font-size: 10pt; display: none">5
<!-- PAGEBREAK -->




<P align="left" style="font-size: 11pt"><B>PEABODY ENERGY ANNOUNCES RESULTS &#150; PAGE 6</B>


<P align="left" style="font-size: 11pt; text-indent: 4%">In the United States, the company will complete its new Bear Run Mine, begin construction on
the Gateway Mine expansion and advance its West Coast Powder River Basin exports initiative. Bear
Run is projected to double production to approximately 6&nbsp;million tons as it continues to expand to
8&nbsp;million tons per year. Construction of the $175&nbsp;million Gateway Mine expansion is expected to
begin in 2011. When complete in several years, the mine&#146;s annual capacity will be expanded
approximately 40&nbsp;percent to 4.5&nbsp;million tons.


<P align="left" style="font-size: 11pt; text-indent: 4%">The company has a number of initiatives under way to expand its presence in the world&#146;s
highest growth markets of China, Mongolia, India and Indonesia.


<P>
<TABLE width="100%" border="0" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="font-size: 10pt">

<TR valign="top" style="font-size: 11pt; color: #000000; background: transparent">
    <TD width="4%" style="background: transparent">&nbsp;</TD>
    <TD width="1%" nowrap align="right">&#149;</TD>
    <TD width="1%">&nbsp;</TD>
    <TD>Peabody recently signed an agreement to source several million tons of coal over
five years from an East Kalimantan, Indonesia mine.</TD>
</TR>

</TABLE>


<P>
<TABLE width="100%" border="0" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="font-size: 10pt">

<TR valign="top" style="font-size: 11pt; color: #000000; background: transparent">
    <TD width="4%" style="background: transparent">&nbsp;</TD>
    <TD width="1%" nowrap align="right">&#149;</TD>
    <TD width="1%">&nbsp;</TD>
    <TD>Peabody and Yankuang Group have entered into agreements to pursue development of the
Wucaiwan Energy Center in Xinjiang, China, which would feature a 20&nbsp;million
ton-per-year surface coal mine, 4&nbsp;billion-cubic-meter coal-to-natural gas facility and
2,000 megawatt supercritical power plant.</TD>
</TR>

</TABLE>


<P>
<TABLE width="100%" border="0" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="font-size: 10pt">

<TR valign="top" style="font-size: 11pt; color: #000000; background: transparent">
    <TD width="4%" style="background: transparent">&nbsp;</TD>
    <TD width="1%" nowrap align="right">&#149;</TD>
    <TD width="1%">&nbsp;</TD>
    <TD>China Huaneng Group, Calera Corp. and Peabody have agreed to pursue development of
an energy campus in the Xilinguole Region of Inner Mongolia. The project would include
a 12&nbsp;million ton-per-year surface mine operated by Peabody and a 1,200 megawatt
supercritical power plant with partial carbon capture and conversion into green
building materials.</TD>
</TR>

</TABLE>


<P align="left" style="font-size: 11pt"><B>OUTLOOK</B>


<P align="left" style="font-size: 11pt; text-indent: 4%">Peabody is targeting first quarter 2011 EBITDA in the range of $325 to $425&nbsp;million and
adjusted diluted earnings per share of $0.45 to $0.65, excluding the impact of foreign tax
remeasurement. First quarter results are expected to reflect continued impacts to sales and costs
related to the record Australian rains, as well as scheduled longwall moves in the United States
and Australia.


<P align="left" style="font-size: 11pt; text-indent: 4%">For 2011, the company is targeting total sales of 245 to 265&nbsp;million tons including 28 to 30
million tons from Australia, 195 to 205&nbsp;million tons from the United States and the remainder from
Trading and Brokerage activities.


<P align="left" style="font-size: 11pt; text-indent: 4%">Peabody Energy is the world&#146;s largest private-sector coal company and a global leader in clean
coal solutions.&nbsp; Its coal products fuel approximately 10&nbsp;percent of U.S. power and 2&nbsp;percent of
worldwide electricity.


<P align="center" style="font-size: 11pt">-End-

<P align="left" style="font-size: 11pt"><B>PEABODY ENERGY ANNOUNCES RESULTS &#150; PAGE 7</B>


<P align="left" style="font-size: 11pt"><FONT style="font-size: 9pt">Certain statements in this press release are forward-looking as defined in the Private
Securities Litigation Reform Act of 1995.&nbsp; These forward-looking statements are based on numerous
assumptions that the company believes are reasonable, but they are open to a wide range of
uncertainties and business risks that may cause actual results to differ materially from
expectations as of Jan. 25, 2011. These factors are difficult to accurately predict and may be
beyond the company&#146;s control. The company does not undertake to update its forward-looking
statements. Factors that could affect the company&#146;s results include, but are not limited to:
demand for coal in the United States and the Pacific Rim thermal and metallurgical coal seaborne
markets; price volatility and demand, particularly in higher-margin products and in our trading and
brokerage businesses; impact of weather on demand, production and transportation; reductions and/or
deferrals of purchases by major customers and ability to renew sales contracts; credit and
performance risks associated with customers, suppliers, co-shippers, trading, banks and other
financial counterparties; geologic, equipment, permitting and operational risks related to mining;
transportation availability, performance and costs; availability, timing of delivery and costs of
key supplies, capital equipment or commodities such as diesel fuel, steel, explosives and tires;
successful implementation of business strategies, including our Btu Conversion and generation
development initiatives; negotiation of labor contracts, employee relations and workforce
availability; changes in postretirement benefit and pension obligations and funding requirements;
replacement and development of coal reserves; access to capital and credit markets and availability
and costs of credit, margin capacity, surety bonds, letters of credit, and insurance; effects of
changes in interest rates and currency exchange rates (primarily the Australian dollar); effects of
acquisitions or divestitures; economic strength and political stability of countries in which we
have operations or serve customers; legislation, regulations and court decisions or other
government actions, including new environmental requirements, changes in income tax regulations or
other regulatory taxes; litigation, including claims not yet asserted; and other risks detailed in
the company&#146;s reports filed with the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC).
</FONT>

<P align="left" style="font-size: 9pt">Included in our release of financial information accounted for in accordance with generally
accepted accounting principles (GAAP)&nbsp;are certain non-GAAP financial measures, as defined by SEC
regulations.&nbsp; We have defined below the non-GAAP financial measures that we use and have included
in the following tables of this release reconciliations of these measures to the most directly
comparable GAAP measures.&nbsp;


<P align="left" style="font-size: 9pt">EBITDA (also called Adjusted EBITDA) is defined as income from continuing operations before
deducting net interest expense, income taxes, asset retirement obligation expense, and
depreciation, depletion and amortization.&nbsp; EBITDA, which is not calculated identically by all
companies, is not a substitute for operating income, net income or cash flow as determined in
accordance with United States generally accepted accounting principles.&nbsp; Management uses EBITDA as
a key measure of operating performance and also believes it is a useful indicator of the company&#146;s
ability to meet debt service and capital expenditure requirements.


<P align="left" style="font-size: 9pt">Adjusted Income from Continuing Operations and Adjusted EPS are defined as income from continuing
operations and diluted earnings per share excluding the impact of the remeasurement of foreign
income tax accounts.&nbsp; Management has included these measures because, in management&#146;s opinion,
excluding such impact is a better indicator of the company&#146;s ongoing effective tax rate and diluted
earnings per share, and is therefore more useful in comparing the company&#146;s results with prior and
future periods.

267.5&nbsp;million for the years ended Dec. 31, 2010 and 2009, respectively. We compute EPS using
a two-class method using an earnings allocation method that determines EPS separately for
common stock and participating securities. As a result, it may not be possible to recalculate
EPS as presented in our condensed consolidated statements of operations.</FONT></TD>

<TR valign="top" style="font-size: 9pt; color: #000000; background: transparent">
    <TD width="1%" style="background: transparent">&nbsp;</TD>
    <TD width="1%" nowrap align="right"><FONT style="font-size: 10pt"><sup>(2)</sup></FONT></TD>
    <TD width="1%">&nbsp;</TD>
    <TD><FONT style="font-size: 10pt"></FONT><FONT style="font-size: 9pt">Reflects income from continuing operations, net of income taxes less net
income attributable to noncontrolling interests.</FONT></TD>
</TR>

</TABLE>

Securities and Exchange Commission.</I>

    <TD align="right">317.4</TD>

<P align="left" style="font-size: 9pt"><FONT style="font-size: 8pt"><sup>(1)</sup> Metallurgical coal sales totaled 2.9&nbsp;million tons and 2.4&nbsp;million tons for the
three months ended Dec. 31, 2010 and 2009, respectively, and 9.8&nbsp;million tons and 7.0&nbsp;million tons
for the years ended Dec. 31, 2010 and 2009, respectively.
<BR>
<sup>(2)</sup> Includes revenue-based production taxes and royalties; excludes depreciation,
depletion and amortization; asset retirement obligation expense; selling and administrative
expenses; and certain other costs related to post-mining activities.
<BR>
<sup>(3)</sup> Includes asset sales, property management costs and revenues, and coal royalty
expense.
<BR>
<sup>(4)</sup> Includes Generation Development and Btu Conversion development costs, costs
associated with post-mining activities, and losses from equity interests.
